correctness.rationale: For every integer n>=5 and degree ell>=0, the addition theorem identifies the Gram as a positive multiple of the evaluation matrix product. A four-sign Walsh decomposition and J(n,2) adjacency spectrum produce exactly four even and two odd sectors with multiplicities adding to n(n-1); antipodal parity gives another n(n-1) zeros. Low-degree Gegenbauer rational factorizations show the only degree-four zero at n=8 of multiplicity n-1 and degree-six zero at n=16 of multiplicity one. Exact checker verifies 55 sector eigenactions and 532 low-degree ranks. The proof is infinite in both parameters and the checker is corroborative.

Higher-degree exceptional dimensions are decided by the formula but not simplified into a global finite exception list.

value.rationale: Full spectra and ranks of exact-degree harmonic sampling on classical type-D root orbits are natural, reusable interpolation invariants. Explicit formulas replace 2n(n-1)-sized eigendecompositions by two/four rational Gegenbauer evaluations, and identify surprising sharp dimension-specific degree-four and degree-six failures. These nontrivial defects address the distinction between harmonic-design vanishing averages and full pointwise interpolation, and are not arbitrary sampled integers.
